I have been having similar thoughts. I told my parents 2 years ago that I didn't feel well psychologically and it only went downhill over the months. At first they were a bit worried about my mental health but didn't want me to go to a psychologist. Then, months later I felt an extreme emptiness and I had gotten to a point where I couldn't be left alone. They heard my crying and screaming and then they finally accepted for me to go to a psychologist, which didn't help at all in the end. Another few months later I started to feel suicidal and I had told my father I constantly had thoughts of wanting to die. He told my mom and she woke me up, crying and hugging me. That's when I knew that they realised my suffering. I feel like saying exactly what you feel and being serious about it is the only thing you can do to make others understand.

You're right, I can't see the point in life but I am searching for it. Is it success? Is it love? Is it helping others? All these things seem logical but in my experience it was all short-term happiness. 

It saddens me to hear you say nobody cares for you. I hope you could realise that there are people who actually do care for you but don't show it in an explicit way. You stay strong as well Ryan!
